notes.1a: Most candidates were able to record sensible, decreasing temperatures for the smaller surface area.
notes.1bi: Similarly most candidates recorded smaller, faster decreasing temperatures for the larger surface area. A few candidates recorded the initial temperature in both beakers before the temperature had reached a maximum and consequently the temperatures at t were less than at t . 0 30 (ii) Units for t and θ were usually correct as were the values for t . Some candidates incorrectly presented the unit for temperature as C° and others failed to give any units for both time and temperature. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2016 (c) Sensible precautions were usually evident although reference to parallax often lacked an explanation.
notes.1di: Several acceptable conclusions were given relating the idea that the larger surface area gave a larger temperature difference in the same time. Weaker candidates were able to calculate the temperature fall but often omitted to mention this was in the same time. Some really able candidates calculated the rate of temperature loss for each beaker.
notes.1dii: Suggested changes to the apparatus were usually sensible as was the effect on the temperature. However, explanations were often weak (e) Most candidates were able to suggest a sensible factor to keep constant, the most popular being a reference to the amount of water.
notes.2a: This was well answered with most candidates recording a set of five increasing values. A few candidates failed to consistently record their values to at least 2 decimal places.
notes.2b: The calculated values of R were correctly given by nearly all the candidates.
notes.2c: Graph work was generally good with correct labelling of both axes with a quantity and a unit. The choice of scale for the V /V was often awkward however with candidates choosing to use the values for V from the table on the major grid lines. This unfortunately led to a  6 scale. Plots were appropriately marked although the expected curved line was occasionally either thick or wobbly.
notes.2d: Many candidates were able to give a simple explanation of the graph shape usually stating that R increased as V increased but usually failed to state that the quantities were not directly proportional. For this to be true the graph would have to be a straight line through the origin.
notes.2e: Only a minority of candidates knew the correct symbol for a variable resistor although the majority knew it had to be connected in a series circuit.
notes.3ai: (ii) Sensible values for h and h with a correct unit were usually given and most candidates were able O I to calculate the magnification M without a unit.
notes.3aiii: Substitution into the equation for f was good and most candidates obtained a value within the required range. Those candidates whose value for f was outside the range were still able to gain partial credit by recording their answer to 2 or 3 significant figures with an appropriate unit.
notes.3aiv: The majority of candidates found it hard to suggest a way to improve the apparatus and often blamed it on their own experimental technique.
notes.3bi: (ii) Many candidates obtained accurate measurements and performed correct calculations throughout these questions.
notes.3biii: The candidates who were familiar with the limits of experimental accuracy usually answered this correctly.
notes.3c: Candidates who are used to looking at images in experimental work were able to suggest a suitable precaution.
